title: Let's cook together
titleJp: {一緒|いっしょ}に{作|つく}ろう

canDos.text: Suggest what to cook in casual Japanese and compare two options (which is quicker, which is better for you).

check.instructions: Your partner (the AI) asks about dinner in casual Japanese. Answer in casual Japanese too: suggest something with the 〜よう form, compare the two dishes with より／のほうが, and give a reason.
check.material:
1. {今日|きょう}の{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}、{何|なに}にする？
2. カレーとパスタ、どっちがいい？
3. どっちのほうが{体|からだ}にいいと{思|おも}う？
rubric: Suggests a dish with the casual 〜よう form (カレーを作ろう, パスタにしよう)
Compares with 〜より〜のほうが (パスタのほうが簡単だよ)
Gives a reason with から
Stays in casual speech (no です/ます)

canDos.text: Read a simple recipe and put the steps in order.

check.instructions: This recipe card for oyakodon (chicken and egg on rice) got shuffled. Read steps A–D, work out the right order, and answer the questions.
check.material:
{鶏肉|とりにく}と{卵|たまご}のご{飯|はん}を{作|つく}ろう！（{二人|ふたり}・{二十分|にじゅっぷん}）
{鶏肉|とりにく}200グラム・{玉|たま}ねぎ{一|ひと}つ・{卵|たまご}{三|みっ}つ・ご{飯|はん}・しょうゆ・{砂糖|さとう}

A　{卵|たまご}を{混|ま}ぜてから、{鍋|なべ}に{入|い}れます。{入|い}れてから、あまり{混|ま}ぜないでください。
B　{鍋|なべ}に{水|みず}としょうゆと{砂糖|さとう}を{入|い}れて、{温|あたた}めます。
C　まず、{鶏肉|とりにく}と{玉|たま}ねぎを{切|き}ります。
D　{鶏肉|とりにく}と{玉|たま}ねぎを{鍋|なべ}に{入|い}れて、{五分|ごふん}ぐらい{待|ま}ちます。
{最後|さいご}に、ご{飯|はん}にかけて{食|た}べましょう！

questions.q: What is the right order of steps A–D?
What does the recipe tell you not to do once the eggs are in?
How many eggs do you need?

canDos.text: Understand your partner's instructions and warnings in the kitchen (don't add the salt yet, don't touch that pan).

check.instructions: You're cooking together and your partner gives you instructions. Listen and answer the questions.
check.material: じゃあ、{野菜|やさい}のスープを{作|つく}ろう。まず、にんじんとじゃがいもを{洗|あら}って、{切|き}って。{玉|たま}ねぎは{私|わたし}が{切|き}るね。あ、そのフライパン、{熱|あつ}いから{持|も}たないで！それから、{塩|しお}はまだ{入|い}れないでね。{塩|しお}は{最後|さいご}に{入|い}れるんだ。{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}からトマトを{出|だ}して。よし、{始|はじ}めよう！

questions.q: What does your partner ask you to do first?
options: Wash and cut the carrots and potatoes

questions.q: Which two things should you not do?
options: Pick up the frying pan, or add the salt now
Open the fridge, or cut the onions
Wash the vegetables, or take out the tomatoes

questions.q: Why shouldn't the salt go in yet?
options: It goes in at the end

canDos.text: Explain why you can't or don't want to eat something, and ask what's wrong when your partner isn't eating.

check.instructions: Part 1: the AI is your partner and notices you're not eating (questions 1–2). Explain why with 〜んです or 〜んだ. Part 2: now the AI isn't eating (line 3). Ask what's wrong and offer to make something else.
check.material:
1. どうしたの？あまり{食|た}べていないね。
2. {何|なに}か{苦手|にがて}なものがあるの？
3. ごめん、{今日|きょう}はちょっと…。
rubric: Explains with 〜んです／〜んだ (お腹が痛いんだ, もうお腹いっぱいなんです)
Gives a clear reason (an allergy, already full, doesn't like it)
Asks どうしたの？ or どうしたんですか when the AI isn't eating
Offers something else with 何か (何か他のものを作ろうか)

canDos.text: Leave your partner a note saying there's nothing in the fridge and asking them to buy something for dinner.

check.instructions: You're going out and your partner will be home first. Look at what's in the fridge, then leave them a note: say there's nothing for dinner, ask them to buy two or three things on the way home, and suggest what to make.
rubric: Says there's nothing for dinner with 何もない or 〜がない
Asks for two or three things with 〜を買ってきてね／買ってきてください
Suggests a dinner idea with 〜よう (カレーにしよう)
Signs off warmly (ありがとう, お願い)

task.goal: Decide on tonight's dinner and who cooks what: agree on one main dish and one side using what you have.
task.outcomeQuestion: What are you having for dinner, who's cooking which part, and what does someone need to buy?

roles.a: Knows what's in the fridge and the cupboard (card A)
roles.b: Knows what they had for lunch and what's on special at the supermarket (card B)

task.infoA:
What's at home (card A):
• Fridge (れいぞうこ): six eggs (たまご), onions (たまねぎ), carrots (にんじん), cheese (チーズ), a little milk. No meat or fish (にくも さかなも ない).
• Cupboard: rice (こめ), pasta (パスタ), curry roux (カレー), a tin of tomatoes.
You're tired, so you'd like something easy (かんたん). You can do the rice and a salad.
Suggest with 〜よう, compare with 〜より〜のほうが, and ask if your partner needs anything (なにか いる？).
task.infoB:
What you know (card B):
• You had pasta for lunch at work today (ひるに パスタを たべた), so you'd rather not have it again. Your partner doesn't know this.
• The supermarket by the station: chicken (とりにく) is half price until 8 p.m., and potatoes (じゃがいも) are cheap. You can stop there on the way home.
• It's cold today and you'd like something warm, like curry or soup.
You don't know what's at home, so ask (なにが ある？) and explain your reasons with 〜んだ.
task.twist: Repeat: the supermarket has sold out of chicken. Decide what you can make with only what's at home, and who cooks it.

scripted.jp: {今日|きょう}の{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}、{何|なに}にする？
scripted.en: What shall we have for dinner tonight?

scripted.jp: {寒|さむ}いから、カレーが{食|た}べたいな。
scripted.en: It's cold, so I feel like curry.

scripted.jp: カレー？でも、{肉|にく}がないよ。{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}、ほとんど{何|なに}もない。
scripted.en: Curry? But we've got no meat. There's almost nothing in the fridge.

scripted.jp: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}。{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}のスーパーで、{今日|きょう}は{鶏肉|とりにく}が{安|やす}いんだ。{買|か}って{帰|かえ}るよ。
scripted.en: That's okay. Chicken's cheap today at the supermarket by the station. I'll pick some up on the way home.

scripted.jp: パスタはどう？パスタのほうが{簡単|かんたん}だよ。
パスタは{昼|ひる}に{食|た}べたんだ。カレーのほうがいいな。
scripted.en: I had pasta for lunch. I'd rather have curry.

scripted.jp: そっか。じゃあ、カレーにしよう。{玉|たま}ねぎとにんじんはあるよ。
scripted.en: Oh, right. Curry it is, then. We've got onions and carrots.

scripted.jp: じゃがいもも{買|か}って{帰|かえ}るね。{他|ほか}に{何|なに}か{要|い}る？
scripted.en: I'll get potatoes too. Do we need anything else?

scripted.jp: ううん、{何|なに}も{要|い}らない。ありがとう。
じゃあ、カレーは{私|わたし}が{作|つく}るよ。
お{願|ねが}い。ご{飯|はん}とサラダは{私|わたし}が{作|つく}るね。
scripted.en: Yes, please. I'll do the rice and a salad.

scripted.jp: いいね！{七時|しちじ}ごろ{帰|かえ}るね。
scripted.en: Great! I'll be home around seven.

capstone.title: Cooking show for two
capstone.brief: Host a two-person cooking show: decide what to make by comparing two dishes, explain the steps, warn each other what not to do, deal with a small problem (something's missing: is there anything we can use instead?), and taste the result.
